definitions.explanation: Eggs beaten and cooked in a pan with stirring, usually served as a breakfast dish. A common Western-style breakfast item in Japan, often paired with bacon, sausage, or toast.

examples.japanese: {朝食|ちょうしょく}にスクランブルエッグを{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I had scrambled eggs for breakfast.

examples.japanese: {牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}を{入|い}れるとスクランブルエッグがふわふわになる。
examples.english: Adding milk makes the scrambled eggs fluffy.

examples.japanese: トーストとベーコンとスクランブルエッグがセットになった{洋風|ようふう}の{朝食|ちょうしょく}が{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like Western-style breakfasts that come with toast, bacon, and scrambled eggs.

notes:
A Western-style egg dish that has become a familiar part of breakfast menus in cafes, hotels, and family restaurants in Japan. Commonly abbreviated in menus and recipes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スクランブルエッグを{作|つく}る: to make scrambled eggs
- ふわふわのスクランブルエッグ: fluffy scrambled eggs
- スクランブルエッグを{添|そ}える: to serve with scrambled eggs on the side
- バター{風味|ふうみ}のスクランブルエッグ: buttery scrambled eggs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {卵焼|たまごや}き: Japanese-style rolled omelet — sweet or savory, cooked in a rectangular pan; a traditional Japanese dish distinct from スクランブルエッグ
- オムレツ: omelet — eggs cooked into a folded or rolled shape, often with fillings
- {目玉焼|めだまや}き: sunny-side up fried egg — a whole egg fried without stirring
- いり{卵|たまご}: Japanese-style scrambled/stirred eggs — finer and drier than スクランブルエッグ, often used in donburi and bento

CULTURAL NOTE:
Although スクランブルエッグ has become popular, いり{卵|たまご} (finely stirred eggs) and {卵焼|たまごや}き remain the more traditional Japanese preparations of cooked egg.
